paper.title: Application of support vector machine modeling for prediction of common diseases: the case of diabetes and pre-diabetes
paper.citation: Yu W, Liu T, Valdez R, Gwinn M, Khoury MJ. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making 10:16 (2010)

assumptions.what: Glucose counts only for people who fasted at least 8 hours (PHAFSTHR >= 8), the NHANES rule for the fasting weights
assumptions.sensitivity: At 6, 7 or 9 hours the fasting groups move by 2 to 8 people; no rule gives all three published counts (table1.json, definition_variants)

assumptions.what: 'Borderline' (DIQ010 = 3) counts as not diagnosed; 'don't know' on family history or hypertension counts as no
assumptions.sensitivity: Borderline as diagnosed gives 1,465 diagnosed; 'don't know' as missing gives 1,262 (table1.json)

assumptions.what: Table 1 counts are complete cases on the scheme I variables (the scheme I totals are the category sums)
assumptions.sensitivity: Without the complete-case rule diagnosed diabetes is 1,525

assumptions.what: Physical activity is PAD320, moderate activity in the past 30 days (yes/no); 'unable' is missing
assumptions.sensitivity: Searched PAD020, PAQ100, PAD200, PAD320 and PAQ180: PAD320 leaves 1,717 and 3,210 scheme II cases and non-cases (paper 1,709 and 3,206); the next best, PAD020, 1,725 and 3,218 (table1.json, pa_variants)

cause.summary: Diagnosed diabetes comes back exactly. The fasting groups are 1, 5 and 5 people off (196, 1,571, 3,272 against 195, 1,576, 3,277); scheme II totals 8 and 4 off. No fasting, borderline or missing-value rule we tried closes the gap. The NHANES glucose files we used carry revision dates of 2009 (1999-2000) and 2007 (2001-2002), so a revision after the authors' download remains possible but could not be tested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Borderline answers counted as diagnosed, or excluded
The glucose files were revised after the authors' download
hypotheses.test: Wayback copies of LAB10AM and L10AM_B from 2015 are listed but could not be fetched from this environment; CDC's documentation gives last revisions of September 2009 and March 2007

table2.label: Table 2, test AUC of the four kernels

assumptions.what: 10 random 80/20 splits (seeds 0 to 9); ours is the median, and a value agrees within two standard deviations over the splits
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper's split is unpublished; one split moves an AUC by about one standard deviation (0.01 to 0.02)

assumptions.what: Weight, height and waist divided by 200, BMI by 100; yes/no coded 1/-1
Polynomial kernel degree 3 and coef0 0, sigmoid coef0 0 (LIBSVM defaults)
Fits inside the grid search stop after 1,000,000 iterations (LIBSVM 2.89 had no limit)
assumptions.sensitivity: On split 0 of scheme I, the linear kernel's search with LIBSVM 3's 10,000,000 limit chose the same C

table3.schemeI.label: Table 3, scheme I (RBF kernel): test, training and 10-fold CV

assumptions.what: The training row is the whole training set, the set whose prevalence the row's PPV and NPV imply
assumptions.sensitivity: On the balanced sample the PPV would be about 0.74

assumptions.what: 10-fold CV reuses the C and gamma of the split's grid search
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not say whether it searched again inside the folds

table3.schemeII.label: Table 3, scheme II (linear kernel): test, training and 10-fold CV

assumptions.what: The training row is the balanced sample, the set whose prevalence the row's PPV implies
assumptions.sensitivity: The row's NPV implies the whole training set instead (text.arithmetic)

assumptions.what: 10-fold CV reuses the C and gamma of the split's grid search
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not say whether it searched again inside the folds

cause.summary: A schematic of a separating hyperplane in a higher-dimensional space; there is nothing to recompute.

fig2.a.label: Fig. 2a, ROC curves of scheme I (pixels, split 0)

cause.summary: The paper's curve comes from one unpublished random split. Two random splits differ by about as much as a curve moved 0.03 in sensitivity (12 px here), so a 2 px score cannot tell our split's curve from the near-miss controls. Fig. 2a in data units (fig2.a.values) compares the published curve with the spread of ours over 10 splits instead.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A different split moves the curve by more than the 2 px tolerance
hypotheses.test: Standard deviation over our 10 splits of the sensitivity at fixed false-positive rates (roc_at_fpr_reps.csv): 0.01 to 0.035, that is 4 to 14 px

fig2.b.label: Fig. 2b, ROC curves of scheme II (pixels, split 0)

cause.summary: As for Fig. 2a: one unpublished split; a different split moves the curve by more than the 2 px tolerance. Fig. 2b in data units (fig2.b.values) compares the published curve with the spread of ours.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A different split moves the curve by more than the 2 px tolerance
hypotheses.test: Standard deviation over our 10 splits of the sensitivity at fixed false-positive rates (roc_at_fpr_reps.csv)

fig2.a.values.label: Fig. 2a, sensitivity at nine false-positive rates (SVM and logistic regression)

assumptions.what: Published sensitivities read off the figure: the median row of the trace in the columns at 1 - specificity 0.1 to 0.9, mapped by the tick marks
assumptions.sensitivity: Tick fit residual under 0.5 px, that is 0.002 in sensitivity; the trace is 1 to 2 px wide
